title: Audit Documentation (Working Papers)
exam_relevance: MODERATELY TESTED - Expect 3-5 questions on CPA AUD exam about documentation requirements, retention periods, ownership, and specific documentation requirements. Understanding proper documentation is essential for all audits.
learning_objectives: Understand the purpose and nature of audit documentation (working papers)
Know what must be documented according to AU-C 230
Master the assembly and retention requirements for audit documentation
Understand ownership of audit documentation and confidentiality requirements
Know the documentation completion date and subsequent changes requirements
Understand specific documentation requirements for various audit areas
Know the requirements for documentation of significant matters and professional judgments
Understand the auditor's responsibilities when facts become known after report issuance

introduction.overview: Audit documentation (also called working papers or workpapers) is the record of audit procedures performed, relevant audit evidence obtained, and conclusions reached. Documentation provides the principal support for the auditor's report and evidence of compliance with auditing standards.
why_documentation_matters: Provides evidence that audit was conducted per GAAS
Supports the basis for auditor's conclusions and opinion
Assists in planning, performing, and supervising the engagement
Facilitates peer review and regulatory inspections
introduction.key_standard: AU-C Section 230 (Audit Documentation) provides the primary guidance on documentation requirements for audits. Similar requirements exist for other attestation engagements under SSAE and SSARS.
introduction.exam_importance: The CPA exam tests documentation requirements including what must be documented, retention periods, ownership, and requirements for changes after the documentation completion date.

definition_and_purpose.definition: Audit documentation is the record of: (1) audit procedures performed, (2) relevant audit evidence obtained, (3) conclusions the auditor reached.
definition_and_purpose.form_of_documentation: Documentation may be in paper form, electronic files, or other media. Increasingly, audits use electronic workpapers.

purposes_of_audit_documentation.principal_support: Provides the PRINCIPAL support for the auditor's report - the documentation must support the opinion issued
purposes_of_audit_documentation.gaas_compliance: Provides evidence that the audit was planned and performed in accordance with GAAS and applicable legal/regulatory requirements
purposes_of_audit_documentation.assists_audit_team: Assists the engagement team in planning, performing, and supervising the audit
purposes_of_audit_documentation.facilitates_supervision: Enables engagement partner and others to supervise work and direct activities
purposes_of_audit_documentation.enables_review: Enables reviewers to review the work performed and evaluate whether appropriate conclusions were reached
purposes_of_audit_documentation.accountability: Provides accountability for the work - shows who did what and when
purposes_of_audit_documentation.quality_control: Facilitates quality control reviews (engagement quality reviews)
purposes_of_audit_documentation.peer_review: Enables peer reviewers to evaluate firm's quality control system
purposes_of_audit_documentation.regulatory_inspections: Allows PCAOB and state boards to inspect audit work
purposes_of_audit_documentation.defense: Provides defense in litigation or regulatory proceedings
purposes_of_audit_documentation.continuing_client: For continuing engagements, provides reference for future audits

definition_and_purpose.exam_emphasis: Audit documentation provides the PRINCIPAL support for the auditor's report and evidence that audit was conducted per GAAS. These are the two most important purposes.

what_must_be_documented.description: AU-C 230 specifies what must be included in audit documentation. The documentation must be sufficient to enable an experienced auditor with no previous connection to the audit to understand the work performed and conclusions reached.

experienced_auditor_standard.definition: An experienced auditor is an individual (within or outside the firm) who has practical audit experience and a reasonable understanding of: (1) audit processes, (2) GAAS and applicable legal/regulatory requirements, (3) the business environment, (4) auditing and financial reporting issues relevant to the industry.
experienced_auditor_standard.key_point: Documentation should be sufficient that someone WITH AUDIT EXPERIENCE (but not on this engagement) could understand what was done and why. You don't need to document every single thought, but must document enough for an experienced auditor to understand.
experienced_auditor_standard.exam_note: The 'experienced auditor' standard is tested - documentation must enable experienced auditor to understand work performed, evidence obtained, and conclusions reached.

general_documentation_requirements.identifying_characteristics: Document sufficient identifying characteristics of items tested or matters inspected to enable item to be located for follow-up. Examples: invoice numbers, dates, amounts, document serial numbers, description of sampling method and criteria for selection.
general_documentation_requirements.who_performed_and_reviewed: Document WHO performed the work and the DATE the work was completed. Document WHO reviewed the work and the DATE of review.
general_documentation_requirements.significant_matters: Document SIGNIFICANT MATTERS arising during the audit, the conclusions reached, and significant professional judgments made in reaching those conclusions.
general_documentation_requirements.discussions: Document discussions of significant matters with management, those charged with governance, and others, including the NATURE of the significant matters discussed and WHEN and WITH WHOM the discussions took place.
general_documentation_requirements.exceptions_or_contradictions: If information is inconsistent with the auditor's final conclusion regarding a significant matter, document HOW the auditor addressed the inconsistency.

specific_documentation_requirements_by_a.overall_audit_strategy_and_audit_plan: Document the overall audit strategy and detailed audit plan including changes made during the audit

risk_assessment.understanding_of_entity: Document understanding of the entity and its environment, including internal control
risk_assessment.identified_risks: Document identified and assessed risks of material misstatement at the FS level and assertion level
risk_assessment.significant_risks: Document significant risks requiring special audit consideration

specific_documentation_requirements_by_a.responses_to_assessed_risks: Document overall responses to assessed risks at FS level and nature, timing, and extent of further audit procedures performed at assertion level
specific_documentation_requirements_by_a.materiality: Document materiality levels: overall materiality, performance materiality, and materiality for particular classes of transactions/account balances/disclosures (if applicable). Document any revision of materiality.
specific_documentation_requirements_by_a.evaluation_of_misstatements: Document summary of uncorrected misstatements (other than clearly trivial) and auditor's conclusion about whether they cause FS to be materially misstated

fraud.fraud_risk_assessment: Document discussions among engagement team regarding risks of fraud
fraud.fraud_risks_identified: Document identified fraud risks and responses
fraud.results_of_procedures: Document results of procedures addressing management override of controls

specific_documentation_requirements_by_a.independence: Document that engagement team and others subject to independence requirements are independent
specific_documentation_requirements_by_a.engagement_quality_review: If an engagement quality review is required, document that the review was performed before the report was issued
specific_documentation_requirements_by_a.related_parties: Document names of identified related parties and nature of relationships
specific_documentation_requirements_by_a.subsequent_events: Document procedures performed regarding subsequent events and results
specific_documentation_requirements_by_a.going_concern: If substantial doubt about entity's ability to continue as going concern, document conditions/events that led to determination, elements of management's plans, auditor's procedures and conclusions
specific_documentation_requirements_by_a.representations: Include in documentation the written representations obtained from management
specific_documentation_requirements_by_a.specific_procedures_confirmations: Document how exceptions in confirmation responses were resolved. If no confirmations sent, document justification.
specific_documentation_requirements_by_a.specific_procedures_inventory: Document results of inventory observation procedures
specific_documentation_requirements_by_a.reliance_on_others: If using work of specialists, component auditors, or internal auditors, document basis for using work and evaluation of work

documentation_of_professional_judgment.requirement: The auditor must document significant professional judgments made in reaching conclusions on significant matters arising during the audit.
what_to_document: The significant matter that required judgment
documentation_of_professional_judgment.example: If auditor concludes that revenue cutoff error is not material, documentation should explain the factors considered (quantitative and qualitative), alternative conclusions considered (e.g., could be material), and why auditor concluded not material.
documentation_of_professional_judgment.exam_importance: Significant judgments must be documented, including the rationale. Questions may test whether adequate documentation of judgment exists.

departures_from_requirements.rule: If the auditor departs from a relevant GAAS requirement (e.g., doesn't perform presumptively mandatory procedure), must document: (1) that an alternative procedure was performed that achieved the audit objective, and (2) the reasons for the departure.
departures_from_requirements.example: If auditor doesn't confirm accounts receivable (presumptively mandatory), must document why confirmations weren't sent and what alternative procedures achieved the objective.

assembly_and_retention.description: AU-C 230 establishes specific requirements for assembling and retaining audit documentation.

documentation_completion_date.definition: The documentation completion date is a date not more than 60 DAYS after the REPORT RELEASE DATE.
documentation_completion_date.report_release_date: The date the auditor grants permission to use the auditor's report in connection with the financial statements (date report is delivered to client).
documentation_completion_date.60_day_rule: The auditor has UP TO 60 days after the report release date to complete the assembly of the final audit file. This is the DOCUMENTATION COMPLETION DATE.
documentation_completion_date.administrative_matters: During the 60-day period, the auditor can complete ADMINISTRATIVE tasks: assembling documentation, checking for completeness, obtaining management representation letter (if not obtained before report date), organizing files, signing off on checklists, etc.
documentation_completion_date.no_new_procedures: The 60-day period is NOT for performing NEW audit procedures (fieldwork should be complete before report date). It's for assembling and organizing documentation.
documentation_completion_date.exam_emphasis: 60 days after report RELEASE date is the documentation completion date. This is frequently tested.

changes_after_documentation_completion_d.general_rule: After the documentation completion date, the auditor must NOT delete or discard audit documentation before the end of the retention period.
changes_after_documentation_completion_d.changes_before_completion_date: Before the documentation completion date, the auditor can make changes to documentation (corrections, additions, deletions) as part of completing the audit file. Must document when and by whom changes were made.
changes_after_documentation_completion_d.circumstances_requiring_changes_after_co: In rare circumstances, the auditor may need to add documentation AFTER the documentation completion date. This occurs when:
situations: Auditor performs new or additional procedures after documentation completion date
Auditor reaches new conclusions after documentation completion date
Rare situations like subsequent discovery of facts requiring procedures

must_document: WHEN and BY WHOM the additions/changes were made
documentation_of_changes_after_completio.cannot_delete: Cannot DELETE existing documentation - can only ADD. If new information contradicts old, document how inconsistency was resolved but keep the original documentation.
documentation_of_changes_after_completio.exam_point: After documentation completion date, can ADD documentation (in rare circumstances) but cannot DELETE. Must document why additions were necessary.

retention_period.minimum_period: Audit documentation must be retained for a period of NOT LESS THAN 5 YEARS from the report release date.
retention_period.five_year_rule: The auditor must retain documentation for at least 5 years. Many firms retain for longer periods (7-10 years is common).
retention_period.state_requirements: Some states require longer retention periods. Auditor must comply with the longer of GAAS requirement (5 years) or state requirement.
retention_period.sec_requirements: For audits of SEC registrants (public companies), SEC requires retention for 7 YEARS.
retention_period.when_retention_begins: The retention period begins on the REPORT RELEASE DATE (not report date or documentation completion date).
retention_period.exam_emphasis: 5 years minimum retention from report RELEASE date for private company audits. 7 years for public company audits (SEC requirement). This is frequently tested.

exam_summary.report_date: Date auditor obtained sufficient appropriate evidence
exam_summary.report_release_date: Date auditor grants permission to use report (delivers to client)
exam_summary.documentation_completion_date: Up to 60 days AFTER report release date
exam_summary.retention_period: 5 years minimum (7 years for SEC clients)
exam_summary.mnemonic: Release → 60 days to complete → 5 years retention (7 for SEC)

ownership.rule: Audit documentation is the PROPERTY OF THE AUDITOR (the CPA firm), not the client.
ownership.client_records: If the auditor's documentation includes client-prepared schedules or records, those remain client property, but copies in the audit file belong to the auditor.
ownership.client_access: The auditor has no obligation to provide audit documentation to the client (though may choose to do so). Some client-prepared supporting schedules may be provided to client upon request.
ownership.exam_principle: Working papers are the auditor's property. This is tested on the exam.

confidentiality.rule: Audit documentation is CONFIDENTIAL. The auditor must maintain confidentiality and not disclose documentation without client consent or legal/professional obligation.
exceptions_allowed_without_consent: Compliance with legal or regulatory requirements (court order, subpoena, regulatory inspection)
Peer review (other CPA firms reviewing the firm's work)
Response to AICPA or state board ethics investigation
Sale or merger of CPA practice (prospective purchaser needs to review documentation)
confidentiality.cannot_disclose: Generally cannot provide documentation to third parties without client consent. This includes banks, attorneys, regulatory agencies (unless required by law), successor auditors (without client consent).
confidentiality.exam_scenario: Bank requests auditor's working papers. Auditor should obtain CLIENT CONSENT before providing. Cannot provide without consent (unless legally required).

working_paper_requests.predecessor_to_successor: Predecessor auditor's documentation belongs to predecessor. Successor auditor should REQUEST access. Predecessor should provide access with CLIENT CONSENT. Standard practice is for predecessor to allow successor to review prior year documentation.
working_paper_requests.regulatory_inspections: PCAOB, state boards, and peer reviewers can access audit documentation as part of inspections/reviews. This is permitted without client consent (professional/legal requirement).
working_paper_requests.litigation: If auditor is sued or subpoenaed, documentation may be subject to discovery. Court can compel production. Confidentiality may not protect against legal process.

requirements: Results of procedures and evaluation of results
For deviations/misstatements: nature, amount, evaluation of effect on audit objective
Expectation and factors considered in developing expectation
Results of comparison of expectation to recorded amounts
Additional procedures performed to investigate significant unexpected differences

reliance_on_others_documentation.specialists: Document specialist's qualifications, nature of work, findings, evaluation of appropriateness of specialist's work
reliance_on_others_documentation.component_auditors: Document component auditor's independence, involvement in component auditor's work, review of component auditor's documentation, conclusion reached
reliance_on_others_documentation.internal_auditors: If using internal auditors, document evaluation of internal audit function, nature/extent of work used, evaluation of internal auditors' work

subsequent_discovery_of_facts.description: If, after the report has been issued, the auditor becomes aware of facts that existed at the report date that might have caused the auditor to revise the report, specific procedures and documentation are required.

requirements_if_facts_discovered.step_1: Determine whether the information is reliable and whether the facts existed at the date of the auditor's report
requirements_if_facts_discovered.step_2: Determine whether persons are relying or likely to rely on the financial statements and auditor's report
requirements_if_facts_discovered.step_3_if_yes: If facts would have changed the report and people are relying on it: (1) Discuss matter with management and those charged with governance, (2) Determine if FS need revision
requirements_if_facts_discovered.step_4: If FS need revision and management agrees to revise: Perform procedures on revision, review steps taken by management to inform users, issue new or amended report
requirements_if_facts_discovered.step_5: If management doesn't revise FS when they should: Notify management and those charged with governance that auditor will seek to prevent future reliance on report, notify regulatory agencies (if applicable), notify persons known to be relying on FS

subsequent_discovery_of_facts.exam_note: If auditor discovers after report issuance that facts existed at report date that would have changed the report, auditor must take action if people are relying on FS. Must document discovery and actions taken.

engagement_quality_review_documentation.when_required: Engagement quality review (also called concurring partner review) is required for: (1) audits of public companies, (2) audits when required by firm policy, (3) other engagements when firm determines review necessary.

must_document: That engagement quality review was performed
Review was completed BEFORE report was issued
Discussions between engagement team and reviewer
Any significant issues raised by reviewer and how they were resolved

engagement_quality_review_documentation.timing: The engagement quality review must be COMPLETED and documented BEFORE the auditor's report is released. Report cannot be issued until review is complete.
engagement_quality_review_documentation.exam_point: Engagement quality review must be completed and documented before report release. This is tested.

electronic_documentation.description: Increasingly, audit documentation is maintained in electronic form. Special considerations apply to electronic documentation.

requirements: Documentation must remain accessible for the retention period
Must maintain integrity of documentation (prevent unauthorized changes)
Must be able to produce documentation in readable form
security_measures: Access controls to prevent unauthorized access/changes
Audit trail showing who accessed and modified documentation
Ability to print or display documentation

electronic_documentation.electronic_signatures: Electronic signatures are acceptable if they uniquely identify the person signing and the date
electronic_documentation.exam_note: Electronic documentation must be secure, accessible, and maintain integrity. Must have controls to prevent unauthorized changes.

practice_problems.question:
An auditor completed the audit of XYZ Company and issued an unmodified opinion on March 15, 2025. The audit report was delivered to the client (report release date) on March 18, 2025.

Required:
1. What is the latest date by which the auditor must complete assembly of the audit documentation (documentation completion date)?
2. What is the earliest date the auditor can destroy or discard the audit documentation (assuming private company)?
3. If this were a public company (SEC registrant), what would be the earliest date the auditor could destroy documentation?
4. On April 10, 2025, the auditor discovers an error in a working paper calculation. Can the auditor correct it? What must be documented?
5. On June 1, 2025, the auditor wants to add additional documentation to clarify a conclusion. Can this be done? What must be documented?

part_1_documentation_completion_date.answer: May 17, 2025 (60 days after March 18 report release date)
part_1_documentation_completion_date.calculation: Report release date: March 18, 2025. Add 60 days = May 17, 2025
part_1_documentation_completion_date.rule: Documentation completion date is a date not more than 60 DAYS after the REPORT RELEASE DATE
part_1_documentation_completion_date.note: The report date (March 15) is not the relevant date - it's the report RELEASE date (March 18) that matters

part_2_retention_private.answer: March 18, 2030 (5 years after March 18, 2025 report release date)
part_2_retention_private.calculation: Report release date: March 18, 2025. Add 5 years = March 18, 2030
part_2_retention_private.rule: Minimum retention period is 5 YEARS from the REPORT RELEASE DATE (for private companies under GAAS)
part_2_retention_private.note: Retention period begins on report RELEASE date, not report date or documentation completion date

part_3_retention_public.answer: March 18, 2032 (7 years after March 18, 2025 report release date)
part_3_retention_public.rule: SEC requires 7 YEARS retention for audits of public companies (more restrictive than GAAS 5 years)
part_3_retention_public.note: Auditor must comply with the MORE RESTRICTIVE requirement - 7 years for SEC clients

part_4_correction_april_10.reasoning: April 10 is BEFORE the documentation completion date (May 17). Before the documentation completion date, the auditor can make changes, corrections, additions, and deletions as part of completing the audit file.
part_4_correction_april_10.must_document: WHO made the change, WHEN it was made, and WHAT was changed. This is normal administrative completion of the audit file.
part_4_correction_april_10.no_special_documentation: Because this is before the documentation completion date, no special documentation of WHY the change was made is required (it's part of normal file completion).

part_5_addition_june_1.answer: Generally NO - June 1 is AFTER the documentation completion date (May 17)
part_5_addition_june_1.reasoning: After the documentation completion date, the auditor generally cannot add documentation except in RARE circumstances where new or additional procedures were performed, or new conclusions were reached.
part_5_addition_june_1.circumstances_allowing: Addition after documentation completion date is only allowed if: (1) auditor performed new procedures, (2) auditor reached new conclusions, or (3) subsequent discovery of facts situation occurred.
part_5_addition_june_1.if_just_clarification: If the auditor just wants to clarify existing documentation without new procedures or conclusions, this is NOT sufficient reason to add documentation after completion date. The file should have been complete by May 17.
part_5_addition_june_1.if_allowed: If there IS a rare circumstance allowing addition, must document: (1) WHEN and BY WHOM added, (2) WHEN reviewed, (3) WHY the addition was necessary, (4) WHAT specific documentation was affected.
part_5_addition_june_1.cannot_delete: Even if addition is allowed, auditor CANNOT delete existing documentation - can only ADD. Original documentation must be retained.

key_takeaways: 60 days after report RELEASE date = documentation completion date
5 years from report RELEASE date = minimum retention (7 years for SEC)
Before completion date: can make changes freely
After completion date: generally NO changes except rare circumstances, and must document extensively

practice_problems.question:
For each scenario, determine whether the documentation is adequate or inadequate, and explain:

Scenario A: Auditor tested 50 sales invoices and found no exceptions. Documentation states: "Tested 50 invoices - no exceptions found." No invoice numbers or identifying characteristics are documented.

Scenario B: Auditor judgmentally determined that an unusual fourth-quarter revenue transaction totaling $2 million was not material to the financial statements (total revenue $100 million). Documentation states: "Unusual Q4 transaction of $2M not material. No further procedures performed."

Scenario C: Auditor performed analytical procedure comparing gross margin percentage to prior year and noted significant decrease. Documentation includes: expectation, comparison to actual, and notes that auditor inquired with management, who explained the decrease was due to product mix changes. Documentation includes no further procedures beyond inquiry.

scenario_A_inadequate.problem: Documentation must include sufficient IDENTIFYING CHARACTERISTICS to enable items tested to be located for follow-up. Simply stating "50 invoices" doesn't identify WHICH invoices.
should_include: Invoice numbers or other identifying characteristics (e.g., Invoice #5001-5050, or specific numbers if judgmental selection)
Description of how the 50 were selected (random, systematic, judgmental)
What procedure was performed (e.g., vouched to shipping documents, agreed to general ledger)
scenario_A_inadequate.exam_principle: Must document sufficient identifying characteristics so items can be located. 'Tested 50 invoices' is insufficient - need to identify WHICH ones.

scenario_B_inadequate.problem: This involves a SIGNIFICANT PROFESSIONAL JUDGMENT (whether $2M unusual transaction is material). Documentation must include: (1) the significant matter, (2) factors considered, (3) alternative conclusions considered, (4) rationale for conclusion reached.
missing_from_documentation: WHY is the transaction unusual? What makes it require judgment?
Factors considered in assessing materiality (quantitative: 2% of revenue; qualitative: nature of transaction, circumstances, users' decisions)
Alternative conclusions considered (could be qualitatively material even if quantitatively immaterial)
Rationale for conclusion that not material despite being unusual
scenario_B_inadequate.should_include: Detailed explanation of judgment: 'Transaction represents 2% of revenue (quantitative benchmark). Considered qualitative factors: [list factors]. Concluded not material because [rationale]. Considered whether qualitative materiality applies but determined [reasoning].'
scenario_B_inadequate.exam_principle: Significant professional judgments must be fully documented with rationale, not just conclusions. 'Not material' is insufficient - must explain WHY.

scenario_C_potentially_inadequate.conclusion: POTENTIALLY INADEQUATE documentation - depends on circumstances
scenario_C_potentially_inadequate.what_is_documented: Documentation includes expectation, comparison, and inquiry with management (good start)
scenario_C_potentially_inadequate.potential_problem: If the variance is SIGNIFICANT and UNEXPECTED, inquiry alone may be insufficient. Must CORROBORATE management's explanation.

assessment.if_variance_minor: If gross margin decrease is small and explanation is reasonable, inquiry may be sufficient. Documentation adequate.
assessment.if_variance_significant: If gross margin decrease is large (e.g., from 40% to 25%), cannot simply accept management's explanation without corroboration. Should document additional procedures performed to verify explanation (e.g., analyze product mix, review sales by product line, test pricing). Without corroboration procedures, documentation inadequate.
assessment.professional_skepticism: Professional skepticism requires corroboration of explanations for unexpected variances. Simply accepting management's explanation without verification is insufficient.

scenario_C_potentially_inadequate.should_add_if_significant: Performed additional procedures to corroborate management's explanation: [list procedures]. Results: [findings]. Conclusion: Management's explanation is supported.
scenario_C_potentially_inadequate.exam_principle: Analytical procedures with significant unexpected variances require CORROBORATION of management explanations, not just inquiry. Must document corroborating procedures.

tip_1_timing_and_retention.description: Memorize the key dates and periods
tip_1_timing_and_retention.report_date: Date auditor obtained sufficient appropriate evidence
tip_1_timing_and_retention.retention_public: 7 years from report RELEASE date (SEC requirement)
tip_1_timing_and_retention.exam_strategy: If question asks about retention or completion date, identify the report RELEASE date first, then calculate from there

tip_2_experienced_auditor_standard.description: Documentation must be sufficient for experienced auditor to understand
tip_2_experienced_auditor_standard.experienced_auditor: Someone WITH audit experience but not on this engagement
tip_2_experienced_auditor_standard.must_enable_understanding_of: Work performed, evidence obtained, conclusions reached
tip_2_experienced_auditor_standard.exam_question: Is documentation adequate? Think: could an experienced auditor understand what was done and why?

tip_3_significant_judgments.description: Significant professional judgments must be fully documented
tip_3_significant_judgments.must_include: Significant matter, factors considered, alternatives considered, rationale for conclusion
tip_3_significant_judgments.not_sufficient: Simply stating the conclusion ('not material,' 'risk is low') without explanation
tip_3_significant_judgments.exam_trap: Documentation states conclusion but not reasoning - this is inadequate for significant judgments

tip_4_changes_after_completion_date.description: After documentation completion date, very limited ability to change
tip_4_changes_after_completion_date.before_completion: Can make changes freely (normal file completion)
tip_4_changes_after_completion_date.after_completion: Can only ADD (not delete) in rare circumstances. Must document extensively: when, who, why, what.
tip_4_changes_after_completion_date.exam_scenario: Auditor wants to add clarification 90 days after report release (past completion date) - generally NO unless rare circumstance exists

tip_5_ownership.description: Working papers belong to auditor, not client
tip_5_ownership.client_access: No obligation to provide to client (but may choose to)
tip_5_ownership.third_party_access: Need client consent to provide to third parties (except court order, peer review, regulatory inspection)
tip_5_ownership.exam_question: Bank requests working papers - auditor should get client CONSENT first

tip_6_identifying_characteristics.description: Must document sufficient detail to locate items for follow-up
tip_6_identifying_characteristics.sufficient: Invoice numbers, dates, customer names, selection method
tip_6_identifying_characteristics.exam_principle: Need to identify WHICH items were tested, not just how many

tip_7_who_and_when.description: Document who did the work and when
tip_7_who_and_when.requirements: WHO performed work, WHEN completed, WHO reviewed, WHEN reviewed
tip_7_who_and_when.exam_note: Documentation must show who did the work and when - this establishes responsibility

common_exam_question_patterns.pattern: Calculate documentation completion date or retention period
common_exam_question_patterns.approach: Find report RELEASE date. Add 60 days for completion. Add 5 years (or 7 for SEC) for retention.

common_exam_question_patterns.pattern: Can auditor make changes to documentation after [date]?
common_exam_question_patterns.approach: Is date before or after documentation completion date (60 days after release)? Before = yes. After = only in rare circumstances.
Check: (1) Identifying characteristics? (2) Who/when? (3) Significant judgments explained? (4) Experienced auditor could understand?
Auditor owns. Need client consent to provide to third parties (exceptions: court, peer review, regulators).

common_exam_question_patterns.pattern: What must be documented regarding [specific area]?
common_exam_question_patterns.approach: Know specific requirements: risk assessment, materiality, fraud discussions, subsequent events, going concern, etc.

memorization_aids.timing_mnemonic: Release → 60 days Complete → 5 years Retain (7 for SEC)
memorization_aids.ownership: WP = Auditor's Property (Working Papers = Auditor's Property)
memorization_aids.experienced_auditor: EA understands WPE: Work, Procedures, Evidence, conclusions
memorization_aids.after_completion: After completion: ADD only (not delete), document WHY

key_concepts: Audit documentation provides PRINCIPAL support for auditor's report and evidence of GAAS compliance
Must be sufficient to enable EXPERIENCED AUDITOR to understand work, evidence, and conclusions
Documentation completion date: up to 60 days AFTER report RELEASE date
Retention period: minimum 5 years from report release date (7 years for SEC clients)
Before completion date: can make changes freely. After: only ADD (not delete) in rare circumstances with extensive documentation.
Working papers are AUDITOR'S property (not client's)
Need client CONSENT to provide documentation to third parties (exceptions: court, peer review, regulators)
Must document: identifying characteristics, who/when, significant judgments with rationale, discussions of significant matters
Significant professional judgments must include: matter, factors, alternatives, rationale
Cannot delete documentation after completion date - can only add in rare circumstances
critical_for_exam: 60 days after report RELEASE date = documentation completion date
5 years retention (private), 7 years retention (SEC public companies)
Experienced auditor standard for documentation sufficiency
Significant judgments must be fully documented with rationale
After completion date: can ADD only (not delete), must document why
Must document identifying characteristics of items tested
common_mistakes: Thinking retention period starts from report date (it's report RELEASE date)
Thinking documentation completion is 60 days from report date (it's from RELEASE date)
Thinking working papers belong to client (they belong to auditor)
Thinking auditor can delete documentation after completion date (can only ADD)
Documenting conclusion without rationale for significant judgments (need full explanation)
Not documenting identifying characteristics (just saying '50 invoices tested' is insufficient)
Confusing retention periods: 5 years for private, 7 for SEC public companies

primary_standards: AU-C Section 560: Subsequent Events and Subsequently Discovered Facts
PCAOB AS 1215: Audit Documentation (for public company audits)
related_standards: QC Section 10: A Firm's System of Quality Control (documentation for quality control)

related_topics: audit_planning_procedures - documentation of audit plan and strategy
